speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We remain optimistic about the medium- to longer-term outlook for Maritime Singapore, which will be boosted by the development of Tuas Port and the growth of our International Maritime Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, there are driving forces we need to prepare for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Governments and companies are reconfiguring supply chains to enhance resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Port operators and shipping lines are integrating adjacent functions and tapping on digitalisation and technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: There is also an increased emphasis on environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The IMO could announce a higher level of ambition to reduce greenhouse gas emissions later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Corporates and individuals are becoming more conscious of their carbon footprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas filed a cut on how we will ensure the relevance and competitiveness of our maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We plan to do so in three ways: enhancing digitalisation, improving sustainability and streamlining business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Twelve maritime 5G base stations will be set up, of which three will be ready by 2023 to support the testing and development of new applications, such as remote pilotage and digital bunkering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA will launch its Next Generation Vessel Traffic Management System in 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This uses data analytics and machine learning to enable our port to safely handle more complex and numerous vessel movements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will launch a tender to develop the system prototype this year, for testing in a real-time operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA worked with the China Maritime Safety Administration to develop and trial standards for the exchange of electronic certificates and port clearance data, to facilitate efficient vessel clearance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The standards will be operationalised for ships travelling between the Port of Guangzhou and Singapore later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: China and Singapore have also submitted a joint paper to the IMO, to promote global adoption of these standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They facilitate trusted and secure data sharing, resulting in better visibility and increased efficiency across the supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked about the development of the Singapore Trade Data Exchange (SGTraDex).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Last year, MPA co-funded a data-sharing pilot for ship supplies procurement and lighterage logistics with SGTraDex, Jurong Port and other partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In 2022, MPA expanded the Industry Digital Plan to all Sea Transport sub-sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: More than 3,000 small- and medium-sized enterprises can now apply for funding support to adopt pre-approved digital solutions and I encourage them to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, for critical information infrastructure in MPA and our port operators, we have upgraded the existing Maritime Security Operations Centre (MSOC) with more advanced capabilities to enhance early threat detection, monitoring, response, information sharing and analysis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As cyber threats evolve, we will continue to expand our capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Next, MPA will establish a Maritime Cyber Assurance and Operations Centre, in collaboration with the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When fully operational in 2025, it will provide real-time security monitoring and disseminate information to mitigate cyber threats, advise on post-incident measures, facilitate information-sharing and training for stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Decarbonising is critical for Maritime Singapore's long-term competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, the transition to a greener future will involve costs and trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Similar to digitalisation, the Government will walk this journey with our companies, but it is also important for businesses and business owners to take action and start to embark on the journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA has made good progress in supporting the electrification of harbour craft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Pilots for the first full-electric ferry by the consortium led by Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited (KOM) and full-electric lighter craft by the consortium led by SeaTech Solutions International will commence later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA is also working with terminal and harbour craft operators to pilot the implementation of charging stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The first charging station will be deployed by Shell at the Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Singapore on Pulau Bukom by the first half of 2023, to support full-electric ferries owned and operated by Penguin International.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will form part of a larger charging infrastructure implementation master plan, which MPA will roll out by 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The transition to a sustainable future will take time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We need to start now to achieve our 2050 net-zero emissions targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, while Singapore does not compete on costs alone, there are areas where we could help businesses to save time and money by reviewing our rules and regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, we are reviewing our transshipment procedures at the land checkpoints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Currently, the transshipment of goods through our land checkpoints at Woodlands and Tuas is considered import to be re-exported.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies must apply for two permits from Customs – one for importing the goods, and another for exporting them, resulting in higher administrative and compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Next, we are reviewing the requirements for exports at our air checkpoint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies are required to screen their cargo before export, which may involve physically opening the cargo for inspection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies with appropriate supply chain security controls in place can apply to the Police, for consideration to receive a reduced level of screening on their cargo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These requirements were put in place for good reasons – to ensure safety and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They have served us well, upholding Singapore's position as a trusted supply chain hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, there is scope to further calibrate the requirement based on risk management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, we could reduce the level of screening for goods exported through Singapore, if they come from overseas companies with strict safety and security processes in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Currently, only Singapore-registered container trucks, and Singaporean or work permit drivers are allowed to enter our container terminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Trucks from Malaysia that are not Singapore-registered and/or have foreign drivers will have to offload their containers outside the port after entering Singapore and load them onto Singapore-registered trucks with Singaporean or work permit drivers, before these containers are allowed to enter our container terminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This double-handling is not productive, as it leads to increased manpower requirements and business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: PSA is working with the industry to allow non-Singapore registered trucks and non-Singaporean drivers under local logistics and haulier companies to access the container terminals and handle containers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They will do this in a phased approach to ensure safety and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The companies and drivers will be subject to PSA's approval, after attending workplace safety training and assessments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Allied Container Services is the first company that PSA has approved under this new arrangement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, while Maritime Singapore does not compete on cost alone, there are areas where we could help businesses to save time and money by reviewing our rules and regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Government will continue to work with industry partners and unions to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, for goods moving between land checkpoints and our seaports, our operators are exploring ways to improve efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Currently, cargo coming in from Malaysia or Malaysian-registered trucks need to be unloaded and loaded onto a Singapore-registered container truck with a Singaporean or work permit driver before they are allowed to enter our container terminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These companies and drivers will be subject to PSA's approval after attending workplace safety training and assessments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With this initiative, local logistics and haulier companies approved by PSA will now be able to directly transport the goods from Malaysia to the container terminals in Singapore, saving time and money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As we adopt a tripartite approach to review our regulations and create a pro-business environment, I also urge companies to make full use of the Government's support to improve their efficiency, including through digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, I am also glad to know that PSA, the Singapore Transport Association (STA), the Container Depot and Logistics Association (Singapore), and Enterprise Singapore have worked together to develop the OptETruck app in November 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It allows the haulier community to exchange data, job pool and integrate solutions, for trips made by their trucks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Currently, each truck makes up to 12 trips a day on average, but about 30% are empty trips.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will also reduce the carbon footprint of the trucks – equivalent to planting up to 300,000 trees a year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At the same time, we need to continue building a future-ready workforce with the right skills and expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In response to Ms Janet Ang, we have put in place several schemes over the years to attract and develop a steady pipeline of maritime talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Last year, I announced that MPA and our tripartite partners would fund a new Sail Milestone Achievement Programme – we call it SailMAP – to support the earnings of our local seafarers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Ms Nur Farhana was one of the 41 seafarers who benefited from this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This helped to offset her training costs for CoC Class 1 and will support her plans to pursue a Master of Science in Maritime Studies at the Nanyang Technological University (NTU).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Gan Thiam Poh that we need a pipeline of local seafarers to support our essential harbour craft sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: SailMAP is designed to deal with the challenges unique to ocean-going seafarers who sail for extended periods while our seafarers within the harbour craft sector can disembark and return home to their families more frequently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA, the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and Workforce Singapore (WSG) have designed training programmes to groom local seafarers to become harbour craft captains and chief engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The programme fees are fully funded, and trainees receive training allowances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA will continue to strengthen the training and support for our local seafarers and work with tripartite partners to attract and retain locals for these roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, I hope our young people will take up maritime-related courses and consider making maritime your port of call.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, I will elaborate on how we will put the community at the centre of our efforts to improve our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A journey is not just about getting from one place to another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During our ForwardSG engagements, participants shared their aspirations for better connectivity, walkability and more inclusive transport infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have made good progress in these areas and plan to do more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Building on residents' feedback, future Silver Zones will have even more safety measures, including Y-junctions, which creates a gradual bend, so that motorists slow down when approaching the junction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides these zones, we are also improving infrastructure for pedestrians to safely cross our roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We prioritised POBs near major transport nodes and healthcare institutions, so that the lifts will benefit commuters with mobility challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond safer road crossing infrastructure, we saw the opportunity to convert some existing road space into footpaths, cycling paths or bus lanes, to make it even safer for the community and improve connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Ms Poh Li San asked for an update.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: So far, we have been working on four projects done through extensive consultation with local stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We completed projects in Havelock Road and Civic District in 2021 and will complete permanent repurposing works at Kampung Admiralty and Tiong Bahru this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At Kampung Admiralty, when we complete the pedestrianisation of a section of Woodlands Ring Road this month, residents can reach the neighbourhood centre more comfortably via covered linkways and widened footpaths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A new bus stop has also been added and from next year, more segments of cycling paths will be ready as part of the wider Woodlands network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At Tiong Bahru, we have worked on pedestrianising and widening footpaths along various streets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Throughout the process, we engaged local stakeholders and residents and will incorporate some of their ideas into the final design, such as creating open spaces for community activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also start two new repurposing projects in the second half of this year at Yung Sheng Road and Choa Chu Kang Terrace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Pedestrianising Yung Sheng Road will enhance pedestrian safety and accessibility between the Taman Jurong Shopping Centre, Market and Food Centre whilst pedestrianising Choa Chu Kang Terrace will make walking to Sunshine Place neighbourhood centre and the upcoming Jurong Region Line more pleasant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue community engagements to implement more such projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond LTA-led projects, LTA has been working alongside other agencies on larger-scale urban rejuvenation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One example is the public-private partnership to revitalise Tanjong Pagar, which Mr Cheng Hsing Yao has asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As part of the effort, LTA has worked with the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) and commercial stakeholders to identify and build new pedestrian crossings, cycling paths and widen some footpaths in the precinct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I visited the area recently, and met teachers and children from a childcare centre at Tanjong Pagar Plaza.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The teachers told me that the children loved playing at a nearby eco-playground, but it was previously very challenging for them to bring the children there due to safety concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As part of the rejuvenation project, LTA built new crossings along Tanjong Pagar Road and Tras Street.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The teachers shared that it is much safer now to walk with the children to the playground while allowing the children to expand their learning beyond the classroom.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These changes go beyond making Tanjong Pagar safer for the young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As a colleague noted, "To LTA, it is a crossing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But to the kids, it is many memories." We will continue to work with stakeholders in Tanjong Pagar to identify and repurpose more stretches of roads to create more space for placemaking and complement the wider urban rejuvenation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is clear that our roads and paths are not just conduits for vehicles and people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They make our towns safer and more vibrant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Friendly Streets initiative builds on LTA's existing efforts to prioritise road space for active mobility, public transport and community uses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This includes Silver and School Zones, Road Repurposing and added features to collectively support more inclusive people-friendly neighbourhoods and gracious communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These will be in high-activity areas and near key amenities in our towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Streets will be made people-friendly in two main ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, by creating a pleasant, inclusive and green environment – with widened footpaths, more greenery, barrier-free crossings and road markings – to inform road users that they are in a Friendly Streets zone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members may also access the handout through the MP@SG Parl app.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As you enter a Friendly Streets zone, you will be greeted by specially designed signages and on-road markings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This encourages all to be more aware and to look out for others.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The streetscapes will also be filled with more greenery and we will consider upgrading bus stops where possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As you move down the street, you will see more people-friendly features, such as pedestrian crossings and cycling paths designed to be used by all.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As you cross the road and enjoy your safer, smoother and greener journey to the Teck Ghee neighbourhood centre, you will likely meet a neighbour or a friend.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We hope you will all greet one another with a friendly smile.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Chairman and Members, this is but a simple example, because we are looking forward to co-designing the details with local stakeholders and bringing in their suggestions for their own neighbourhoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Together, we will not just build roads, but also memories.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Moving to Mr Melvin Yong's suggestion on only allowing lorries fitted with seat belts on the rear deck to be sold in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As previously shared, original equipment manufacturers had concerns that seatbelts on rear seats will create new safety risks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the chassis and rear deck of lorries are separately put together, they will not be strong enough to anchor seat belts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) will not fit seat belts onto the rear deck of new lorries, nor vouch for the safety of such lorries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On phasing out lorries that can ferry workers on the rear deck as the lorries' COE expire, this could be disruptive for many industries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I would also like to clarify that many lorries with COEs expiring within the next five years will not have reached the end of their statutory lifespan of 20 years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over 60% of lorries with COEs that expired in 2022 had their COEs renewed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our "Walk Cycle Ride" vision remains at the heart of our future land transport system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Still, we understand that some need a car for various reasons.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When private transport is required, we encourage drivers to choose cleaner energy vehicles, especially EVs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have been making steady progress to make charging points more accessible and reduce range anxiety among potential EV drivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This includes around 1,600 publicly accessible and 1,200 private charging points, with the remainder for BlueSG users only.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The EV Common Charger Grant was launched in July 2021 to co-fund charger installation costs in private condominiums.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The extension complements recent amendments to the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act that make it easier to pass resolutions to install chargers and further boost charger deployment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA and URA awarded a pilot tender in 2021 to deploy more than 600 charging points in over 200 public carparks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The five successful tenderers will simultaneously install chargers all across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Responding to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, these charging points will support the charging needs of both electric cars and electric motorcycles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the usage of charging points, utilisation rates for EV charging points under the pilot tender are around 8%, on average, over the last month.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is within expectations, because the Government is frontloading charger deployment in the early years of EV adoption to give drivers the assurance to choose EVs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA works closely with EV charging operators to plan charger deployment, based on local demand, to deploy slightly ahead of expected demand, but not over-deploy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about the costs of EV charger deployment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the tenders at public car parks, EV charging operators bear the cost of the charging equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA, the Energgy Market Authority (EMA) and HDB are conducting an advanced engineering study to assess electrical upgrades required to support residential EV charging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government will bear the cost of these upgrades and, eventually, recover this cost through a tariff on EV charging operators and users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The deployment of EV charging points on the ground will be planned and managed by EVe, a fully-owned subsidiary of LTA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also convened the EV Steering Group, an interagency committee to coordinate the Government's charger deployment policy across key agencies, such as LTA, HDB, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and EMA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This Steering Group, co-chaired by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng and myself, will focus on three "Cs".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Most of the charging points that we are deploying islandwide will be slow chargers at residential estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, we are also exploring where fast chargers can be deployed to provide an option for high-mileage users, such as taxi drivers, who may need top-ups on the go.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The ramp-up in charging points is necessary to serve Singapore's growing EV population, especially among light goods vehicles, or LGVs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This suggests that existing incentives, such as the Commercial Vehicle Emissions and Early Turnover schemes, are effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As e-LGVs have lower operating costs than diesel LGVs, many fleet owners have realised that it is cheaper to operate an e-LGV over its lifecycle.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For heavier vehicles, we will engage fleet owners to see how we can facilitate their transition to a greener fleet.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA has been engaging EV drivers on their driving and charging experiences and is working with operators to foster socially responsible EV charging norms.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many EV charging operators today are considering measures to deter lot-hogging, such as idle fees.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we must do more to develop gracious charging etiquette among EV users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, LTA is planning a citizen engagement exercise to develop ground-up recommendations on nurturing good charging etiquette.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will support the industry in training the workforce in areas, such as the EV charging standards.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our Steering Group, together with EVe, will engage industry stakeholders and the public to support a safe and sustainable EV transition.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Chairman, I will now move on to point-to-point, or P2P, transport, which plays an integral role in complementing other transport modes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Ms Yeo Wan Ling noted, the P2P sector and drivers' livelihoods were significantly impacted during the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as Singapore transitioned towards an endemic COVID-19 norm, P2P trips recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels in 2022.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, fuel prices moderated over 2022, mitigating the impact of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on drivers' costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With this ridership recovery, P2P drivers have seen improved earnings and incomes returning to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Whilst demand for P2P services has increased, there are now fewer P2P drivers, as some had left the sector during the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, with fewer P2P drivers available, riders experience high surge fares and longer waiting times, especially during the late evening or night.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Mark Chay asked for an update.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The tight supply of P2P drivers reflects the manpower shortage in many sectors post-COVID-19 and the industry will require time to adjust to demand for P2P rides.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For now, P2P operators have shared that they are recruiting more new drivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Operators are also rolling out features, such as "hotspot navigation" to alert drivers to areas with more booking requests, to better match demand and supply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some have reintroduced ride-sharing services, where riders going to similar destinations can share a ride and be served by one driver.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This allows the existing limited pool of drivers to serve more riders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the Government's part, LTA will work with operators to reduce the time to process vocational licence applications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As operators tackle new challenges faced by the sector, we will continue working with the industry stakeholders and drivers to address issues, ensuring drivers' livelihoods, addressing P2P availability and looking ahead to shifts in the sector's landscape.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over time, we have seen structural shifts in the needs of our land transport system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: During our ForwardSG engagements, we heard some youths sharing aspirations to have the option to use a car, without necessarily owning a car.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Ms Poh Li San shared, car sharing may be an option for people who only require a private vehicle from time to time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Car sharing refers to the short-term leasing of cars, typically for less than a day.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are several operators, like Getgo and BlueSG.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Based on preliminary engagements with operators last year, we understand that there is growing demand for car sharing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA will work with operators to better understand the needs and potential role of the industry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Chairman, in conclusion, we look forward to working with the community to co-create friendly streets, making our towns safer and more vibrant.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As we reimagine our road space, we also encourage the use of more sustainable alternatives, such as EVs and shared modes of transport.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through these initiatives, we can work together to create a more people-centric land transport system for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will first provide an update on the progress of our Active Mobility, or AM, landscape, before elaborating on our efforts to promote inclusive journeys and a sharing culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the last few years, the AM landscape has evolved significantly, with more people taking up active modes of transport, such as walking and cycling.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is a good thing, as AM is the greenest, cheapest and healthiest mode of transport available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how we intend to curb the illegal use of Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: E-scooters have been required to be registered since 2019 and be inspected every two years since 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2021, we also introduced import controls to stem the inflow of non-compliant motorised devices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: E-scooter and power-assisted bicycle, or PAB users, are required to pass the mandatory theory test before they can ride their devices in public spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our AM enforcement officers are deployed daily to ensure that our paths remain safe and to take action against errant riders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA also leverages technology, such as mobile closed-circuit television cameras, to augment its enforcement efforts, and conducts joint operations with other agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With that, I am glad to say that we have made good progress in improving AM safety over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But we need to sustain this good progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to work closely with our partners and communities to do so, such as the AM Community Ambassadors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since our call for volunteers last November, a few cycling interest groups, such as BPR Cycling Club and RIDERS Arena, have registered their interest with us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA has started to onboard these new volunteers last month and I look forward to the contributions from all our ambassadors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Moving forward, we will work closely with new and existing ambassador teams to expand outreach activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For those who are interested to join us, you can indicate your interest through the LTA website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the AM landscape continues to grow rapidly, we are monitoring new trends closely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together with the Active Mobility Advisory Panel, or AMAP, we are strengthening our regulatory framework while building a more inclusive culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: AMAP comprises a diverse mix of representatives of different stakeholder groups, such as seniors, youths, people with disabilities, cyclists and motorists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This allows us to consider various perspectives to ensure that our rules remain relevant and effective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Mr Eric Chua mentioned, AMAP recently reviewed the use of cargo bikes, trikes, rider-only tricycles and recumbents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While these devices are still used in small numbers locally, it is timely for our regulations to be reviewed, to ensure that the rules of usage are clear and that they can be used safely in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Panel engaged a wide range of stakeholders and has provided a set of balanced recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As earlier mentioned by Minister Iswaran, the Government has accepted AMAP's recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In our evaluation, we have aimed to balance between facilitating the use of more devices and ensuring the safety of all path and road users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Non-motorised devices will be subject to the existing device criteria when used on paths, including weight and width limits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Motorised versions of these devices will continue to be disallowed on paths and roads until recognised safety standards are available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In consultation with MHA and the Traffic Police, we will also be introducing new limits for all AM devices used on roads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope to continue facilitating such devices that have been used on the roads in Singapore for a long time with no major safety issues, while preventing proliferation of overly large devices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will raise public awareness and safe use of these newer devices, and I thank all stakeholders who have contributed to this review.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: AMAP is currently reviewing the safe and responsible use of personal mobility aids, or PMAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: PMAs help individuals with mobility challenges, including those who have non-visible medical conditions, such as arthritis, that prevents them from walking long distances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, there have been reports of potential abuse and misuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to ensure that these devices remain accessible to those who need them, but at the same time, it is also important to ensure that they are being used safely on our paths and that they do not detract from encouraging healthier lifestyles, such as walking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: AMAP is in the midst of engaging stakeholders and will submit its recommendations later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, I will now say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   This year, we will review the regulations of PMAs, such as motorised wheelchairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Thus far, we have taken a light touch on regulations in order to remain inclusive, to cater for elderly who may have mobility issues and require such devices to commute.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, there have been recent feedback that seemingly fit and younger people were seen riding motorised wheelchairs in the neighbourhood and even on the roads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There are also concerns on fire safety when modified PMAs are being charged.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will strike a balance between ensuring the safety of public paths and the accessibility of people who need these devices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I also urge everyone to walk when you can.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The less we walk, the weaker our legs will become.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even if our legs are weak, do not become over-reliant on motorised wheelchairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The key is to stay healthy and strong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English): Ms Yeo Wan Ling shared some concerns of delivery riders and asked if we could consider allowing different classes of AM devices, such as heavier ones, to be used on roads and paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We note these concerns and will continue to review our existing regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But they have to be balanced with concerns of safety raised by other path and road users, and also by Members of the House.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The limits were put in place in consideration of the power of such devices and the potential dangers that they pose to other users in the event of an accident.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To support greener commutes, we are pressing ahead to implement more cycling paths islandwide.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They will be constructed progressively across all towns over the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Residents living in the East and North-east regions can expect more comprehensive cycling path networks from 2024.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On Ms Ng Ling Ling's request, we will first prioritise connectivity to transport nodes and key amenities, before expanding to other areas progressively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Nonetheless, the relevant agencies are studying the area and would be happy to work with her.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For those living in the West and Central areas, including the Nanyang Division which Mr Ang Wei Neng had asked about, we will be rolling out plans to build cycling paths there as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Residents in these areas can look forward to better connectivity within and between these towns when these are progressively implemented.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is an ambitious programme, especially when we have to construct most of the paths in estates which are already very built up and where space is scarce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Finding space can be a challenge, and in some cases, we need stakeholders' support to make way for new cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, LTA recently worked with five different schools in Bukit Panjang to reconstruct their school boundary walls and fences to create space for cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During construction, we will also take the opportunity to dovetail with other infrastructural works where possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, as much as we are trying to accelerate the programme, we seek Members' and Singaporeans' patience and understanding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Apart from these intra-town paths, we are also looking into options for cyclists who prefer longer-distance cycling commutes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One such example is the North-South Corridor, designed with a cycling trunk route that would connect AM device users directly from the Northern region to the city.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Poh Li San and Mr Saktiandi Supaat may wish to know that where space allows, we try to have dedicated cycling paths for AM device users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Central Business District (CBD) is a good place to do so and Senior Minister of State Amy Khor had previously mentioned about our plans to rejuvenate Tanjong Pagar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, given Singapore's land constraints, it is not possible to always build separate paths for different users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will all need to be prepared to share our spaces, and to do so graciously and safely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, LTA launched the Sunday Cycling Lane trial along West Camp Road in Seletar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Five months into the trial, we observed that cyclists and motorists have co-existed well by keeping to their respective lanes, and the journey time of buses and other vehicles travelling along West Camp Road have also not been affected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Into the last month of the trial, LTA will conduct surveys with stakeholders and gather feedback, before deciding whether the lane would be permanent or enhanced further.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Moving forward, LTA is studying other stretches which are frequented by on-road cyclists and where vehicular traffic is relatively low.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This would also be subject to consultation with other agencies and engagements with relevant stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chair, we are also stepping up efforts on inclusivity in public transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Mr Ang Wei Neng notes, many Singaporeans are keen for our transport system to be more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members of the public can bring people who lose their way to any of these major public transport nodes and enlist the help of our public transport staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beginning last year, we have also fitted Braille signs at the queue rails of each boarding berth at bus interchanges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These signs allow commuters with visual impairments to know which bus services are available at the berth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the elderly and families with young children, we have built accessible changing rooms and family toilets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: All these rooms with automatic sliding doors will come with audio announcements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These will be useful for visually-impaired commuters who can also just wave a hand to lock the door.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These infrastructure upgrades have been included in new bus interchanges since last year and will be added to existing bus interchanges that are slated for upgrading where practicable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Typically, a new MRT station brings about 800 metres of covered linkways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With more than 60 new MRT stations, including interchanges, coming up in the next decade, our network of covered linkways will only continue to grow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to work closely with other agencies to enhance the walking experiences of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we make improvements in hardware, we have also continued to foster a caring commuting culture in public transport, primarily through the Caring SG Commuters movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Another 700 volunteers are undergoing the online training course at their own pace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Anyone can enrol for the online training for free at the Caring Commuters website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Moving forward, we will actively increase outreach efforts and engage our existing partners to promote inclusivity on public transport and enhance outreach to private sector organisations, to raise awareness and recruit more Caring Commuter Champions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our Public Transport Operators (PTOs), who are the frontline touchpoint for commuters, are our close partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They have worked closely with Social Service Agencies to develop inclusive initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One of the initiatives was the Helping Hand scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We started with a sticker or card displaying "May I have a seat please?" to help commuters be aware of those who need a seat more, especially those whose medical conditions may not be obvious.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This message has been expanded to the entire bus and train network across all PTOs, and commuters who need these stickers or cards may request for them at bus interchanges and MRT stations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We encourage commuters to exercise graciousness and give up their seats – and not just priority seats – to fellow commuters who need them more and will put up posters at prominent locations as visual reminders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The new messages will be progressively rolled out, starting with the bus network, and publicity will be done on various online and out-of-home platforms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, Sir, we have made good progress in our AM landscape over the past few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will keep up the momentum to provide more inclusive and sustainable modes of transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Nonetheless, more can be done to achieve our goal for a gracious and sharing community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: No matter your mode of transport – whether you choose AM or public transport – let us look out for one another, so that everyone can move around Singapore safely and with ease.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Minister, my cut to MOT this year is a follow-up to my colleague, Mr Faisal Manap's Adjournment Motion of October 2021 on motorcycle ownership and his other Parliamentary Questions on high motorcycle COEs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I note the Minister's point about finance as a service offered by many motorcycle dealerships and I recognise the role that it plays.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, the prospect of speculative bidding of motorcycle COEs has always been a concern of the public.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I will not go through the newspaper articles that can substantiate this concern.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Minister said that the violations of motorcycle financing would be subject to the Hire Purchase Act.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But the Hire Purchase Act comes under the purview of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It pertains to the second point of my cut.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I use 10 years because it is the lifespan of a COE, even though I note that the practice had been stopped in 2017.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Leader of the Opposition for his questions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Actually, these two questions straddle the gamut of almost all the issues; so, they are deceptive in their apparent simplicity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Perhaps, I will start with the second point on COEs and allocation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think what the Leader of the Opposition is driving at is whether there is a way to re-allocate some of the old COEs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that was the point he made earlier because of the old system, which was discontinued in 2017.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, let me say and I want to reiterate this point, I omitted to mention Mr Fasial Manap's Adjournment Motion, but as I said, I do not think any one party here has a monopoly on the care and concern for motorcycle owners.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We all do, we are all endeavouring to help and the question is: how to best achieve that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have done this because of the overall interest in terms of the liveability of our city and ensuring that even our roads, the flows, the vehicular flows can be sustained going forward, taking into account road development and all the other modes of transportation that we are developing.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have to take it from some other category in order to give it to a more critical category.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Leader of the Opposition's proposal is to take it from, I think, Cat E, or – I cannot remember where.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But there have been similar arguments made in this House for other categories – whether it is for Cat A, whether it is for Cat C, commercial.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, how do we decide then where to take it from, where to allocate it, how much to allocate and how do you measure that the outcome has been successful?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because, clearly, the intent here is that – and I am reading into the Member's comment – unless prices soften, the desired objective has not been served.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we have to look at any change we make to the COE system holistically, for all the reasons I have just highlighted.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To propose one particular dimension for modification without looking at the systemic implications, I think would be remiss on our part.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But, as I have said, having said that, we have been prepared to take measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have, not only the systemic measures to help motorcycle owners in terms of costs, but also some of the more recent measures to curb any potential speculative behaviour on the part of motorcycle dealers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And, as I said, I hope buyers and dealers will take note of this when making their decisions on bidding and buying for Cat D.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The first point that he raised was the financing elements.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, we should all be very focused on our core mission.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And the mission in LTA and for MOT is to make sure that we have agreed on a policy for managing the population of vehicles and we have an allocation mechanism through the COE, and we should ensure that that is working to the best of our ability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, financing is essential because most buyers of vehicles, generally, do need financing assistance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Whether we can study further, whether there are any other alternatives, I would say that this is actually better left to the market and to industry players to respond.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because in the end, LTA or the Government is not in a unique position in any way, or even in a position where we have special insights into this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member himself has highlighted this, there is a cooperative and so on – the practices, the mechanisms exist, in other contexts perhaps.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And it is really best left to the market.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the point of how do you re-allocate that, I recognise the difficulty in doing so, particularly in the context of a zero-vehicle growth policy.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I think the other context to consider, and I make this appeal to the Minister, is the landscape with regard to what has happened since 2017, and today – insofar as a burgeoning of the gig economy and the need for lower-income Singaporeans to have an affordable mode of transportation to deliver food and whatever else, has changed.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, that was the context in which I raised the argument that covered a previous policy of LTA, which was to take COEs from the motorcycle Cat D and put it to the Open Category.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I was wondering whether there could be some considerations because of the landscape, to see whether it is feasible to consider a transfer back.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In my cut, I use the word "equity and fairness".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not meant to dilute the Minister's response of the larger task of re-allocation from other categories as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the point of the market, indeed, ultimately, that is the bedrock that has to sustain financing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But in view of the ForwardSG exercise, I think there was an exercise which looked at the prospect of cooperatives partnering businesses to better manage finance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am wondering whether the Ministry could nudge our cooperatives to consider providing loans for lower-income Singaporeans, so as to ensure that the arbitrage that motorcycle financers gain is not overly large, to the detriment of lower-income Singaporeans who need these bikes in the first place.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, on the point on re-allocation, some data points are useful.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if we talk about changed circumstances that warrant considerations specifically for motorcycles, because of, say, delivery, the same might apply to Cat A cars, for example, because they are used for Grab, or those kinds of platform services.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What I am trying to illustrate is, I do not think we have a disagreement in terms of wanting to help.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we have to be very clear that in our desire to do so, we do not throw the baby out with the bathwater.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: When the prices were lower, we were not debating these issues in the same way.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we have to understand clearly what is the driver or what is causing it, and be prepared to respond if, in fact, there are structural or systemic issues that we think need to be resolved.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am just advocating having a care and also trying to present the larger perspective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The second point is, the point has been made, on "equity and fairness", and I think "equity and fairness" depends on where you stand and whom you are advocating for.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I can assure the Leader of the Opposition that I have had many who have advocated for other groups with equally meritorious claims for favourable allocation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think it is a subjective discussion, one that we need to take into account, we need to take serious consideration of, in terms of the circumstances.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we should also make sure that if we are going to make a systemic change, it is one that we can then not just defend, but also make sure that we can sustain it in the long run, because it is warranted, in the manner that we have just discussed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the possibility: so, now, it is beyond MTI; it has gone to the cooperatives and whether we can ask them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I just want to come back to what I said at the start, which is that, in the end, there are various market mechanisms.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We should encourage it; I fully agree with that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I just want to make that point.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just have two clarifications for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think that it is a great project.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My question is, instead of it being just a standalone project with a committee, for constituencies that are entering into a major Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP), can it also be a standard, so that we can have a more collective and integrated plan for our residents.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second clarification is for the installing of lifts in the POBs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am really glad to hear that it will be expanded in recognition of our ageing population.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On one side is a very densely populated residential area but on the opposite side, is an industrial area.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the consultation with LTA, I have been informed that because the density is not high enough to justify this, it will be considered.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would just like to ask if there is a hope for it, so that my residents can hope for one day having the lift there as well because they are also ageing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the Friendly Streets pilot, we are wanting to work with the local community and will form a committee.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if you have an NRP going on, then the relevant stakeholders can also be involved.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, the Friendly Streets initiative is really about integrating; looking at an entire zone and then putting in place the various projects that we may have, whether it is a School Zone, Silver Zone, your NRP as well as other initiatives to make the area more friendly for users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the POBs, it is a coveted scarce commodity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, definitely, Members can continue to hope for it and we will take note of this.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Minister Iswaran mentioned the mandatory switch to EVs by 2025 for the airside vehicles at the airport.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: These airside vehicles are mainly owned by private companies or listed companies, the ground handlers.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This will add new cost pressures, with new vehicles and electricity cost for these companies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The second question is for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We have about half a million private vehicles in Singapore and there are plans to increase to about 60,000 EV charging points islandwide by 2030.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I have a question in my cut regarding whether there are plans to convert the existing petrol stations to support EV charging.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hopefully, we may also use some of these assets to convert them into fast-charging EV stations in the future, to augment the 60,000 EV charging points required nationwide.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The third clarification is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng who shared about the trial of cycling zones in Seletar West Camp.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I am sure the cyclists will appreciate it.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I would just like to know, following the successful five-month trial, whether there would be plans to extend to more areas, especially the longer stretches, like those in the Lim Chu Kang area?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The kiosks – about 180 all round – about half are on Temporary Occupation Licences or short leases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, depending on how the demand for EV chargers pans out – basically, now, there are already petrol kiosks that have installed EV chargers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For some, it is a question of business model and how they transit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For others, depending on whether there is demand in that specific location and so on, some may actually transit out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will have to look at this as the EV charging network builds up and demand for EV cars increases.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a time-based cycling lane, so it is actually a road lane for normal vehicles at other times.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As we have limited land space, road space, we cannot always build dedicated paths.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So far, it has been five months since we started it.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As I have said, the feedback and the observations have been positive.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are also going to do a proper survey among the users to get feedback on how the scheme could be improved.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That would give us the confidence to explore other areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These would be areas that are already used by road cyclists, because we want them to go where they want, but at the same time, at a time or day where normal road traffic is already low, so that it does not have a high potential for clashes to happen.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For the Lim Chu Kang area, yes, we will look at that and we hope that we will be able to do more in other areas as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, Ms Poh Li San has raised an important point regarding the cost impact.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is why, in coming up with this recommendation on electrification from 2025, it is really about focusing on the replacement of the airside vehicles.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then, the question of relative cost, I would say that there are a few things happening here at the same time.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have already seen that over the last several years as EV manufacturing and supply have scaled up.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the other side of it, any cost associated with emissions also has to be factored in.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, in Singapore, we have already spoken about our carbon tax trajectory.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, when you factor all of these in, take these into account, in general, it is a manageable transition without imposing undue cost, and I think the businesses also see the competitive value proposition of doing so.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to ask about two and a half questions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Regarding Friendly Streets, when you co-create, does it involve the option of having covered linkways?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The reason I ask is because some areas are beyond MRT stations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will covered linkways be part of the suite of options that can be chosen by the committee?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is with regard to my cut on the Ministry's plans to roll out affordable electric motorcycles as part of the sustainability efforts in our land transport system.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What does it mean for Singapore and can we have an assessment of the possible early adoption incentives for electric motorcycles?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For Singaporeans who want to get electric motorcycles, will there be incentives?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My "half" question is with regard to electric buses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have met residents who mentioned that they really want to have electric buses because they are quieter, they are less noisy, especially for those living on the second, third floors of HDB blocks, facing bus stops.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, the target is half of the buses by 2030, possibly, all by 2030, if it is possible?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Your "half" question was the request for Toa Payoh.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I can answer that "half" question on the linkway.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is why we are forming a committee and getting local stakeholders involved.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will take all suggestions and ideas into consideration and study this as part of the Friendly Streets initiative.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Obviously, we will have to look at the viability and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am tempted to say that every street is a friendly street.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You have the plug-in charger types, but they are largely the more high-end type of motorcycles.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There are the battery-swapping models, which seem to be becoming more common in other markets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, this is the reason why we are conducting these pilots.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that by learning from them, we will be able to come up with the appropriate regulations on that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In terms of affordability, my expectation is they will probably end up, like in cars, with a spectrum of such electric motorbike solutions available in the market.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, you can already see it in other parts of the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is already quite a bit of an acceleration over the last one to two years, because we decided we have to move.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What I think I would say is: let us get this first tender out, let us run in the system a bit more, because what we have had up to now are pilots and trials.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We now need to do this at scale and understand the implications, because when you ramp up and it goes up to half or more of your fleet, the implications are quite different from running a small-scale pilot.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I just want to assure the Member that we share his enthusiasm for this transition.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have three clarifications for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor and one quick clarification for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: The Chairman
text: But we need time for the response as well.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: First, I would like to ask very quickly, does the Government have any plans for alternate renewable energy choices for EV drivers besides natural gas?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Related to this, has the Government studied the feasibility of having some of the public chargers be powered by solar panels fitted on the multi-storey car parks (MSCPs), at least in part?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My second clarification is whether the Government is concerned with the slower conversion of heavier vehicles and lorries to EVs and will it affect our plans for 2030 and beyond.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The third clarification for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor is whether the Government will actively engage logistics companies directly on their plans to convert to EVs to speed up the process.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My clarification for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng – I thank him for the reply on PMDs – I just want to request that the Government continue its enforcement, engagement and public education efforts in respect of PABs as well because it is common to see electric bicycles beating red lights, cycling against traffic, not wearing helmets.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I also see many cruising on electric bicycles without having a pedal at all, which is not consistent with the LTA requirement that the motor power can only cut in when the cyclists start to pedal.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, it suggests that there is still a lot of illegal PABs running around.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On using cleaner renewable energy for electricity generation, that is actually under MTI.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On MSCP solar panels, there is already a scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: HDB also has a scheme – the SolarNova scheme – to put solar panels on rooftops and, I am sure, if it is possible, for MSCPs too.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, that is also not under this Ministry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On logistics companies' transition to cleaner vehicles, we are working with them, but it is now limited by the availability of this kind of vehicles, in terms of technology.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That would include those, which the Member had also observed, where they were not pedalling but they were able to move.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, if these are caught, they would be confiscated.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As for enforcement on the roads – speeding, beating red lights and so on – we hold joint enforcement with the Traffic Police.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In areas like Park Connector Networks (PCNs), we hold joint operations with the National Parks Board officers as well.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We want all users to understand the rules and abide by the rules.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
